title: Jam sessions at the union hall and sitting in with bands
summary: One long block about travelling, the union hall as a conservatory, and sessions.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Liotta Lyon was down there, or recorded with Al Hood when he was on this, what you call him here, Liotta Lyon. He, when you were going all over like I was, it was nice to meet everybody. You see, those bands like Jimmy Noon and all of them, they were coming down in northern part of Louisiana before they started coming here. You understand? You see all them bands used to come down there. See because everybody would turn out, you know it's like the Saints football game, everybody would turn out with all those bands. You understand? And there used to be some bad boys around there. You see, at the last, I was, when I was swimming with that thing every night, you see, things just come to me. I swooned at a banjo and stuff every night. And of course what I did today ain't nothing to what I can do. Maybe you might not believe me, or what the man's swimming, but you know you get rusty when you don't fool with them. You understand? You're like anything else. Or Tatum, and all that fun. Well, you see, after I learned how to play, and I wanted to see those guys, you understand? And pick up on their songs just like a guy, Duke Ellison and some of them come in town, well, they would have. It's like Dream, but he don't use no Apple Fire on his guitar. He's got a, what's he called, made that guitar for him. He used to take the certain type of wood that they would use to make the Freddie Green with Connelly and all of them. And I was a standby band, or rather Sidney Keith's band was a standby band, but Sidney couldn't play as much as me. And I got in there and played Serena and a couple of things like that and all those things. You see, it's just like a lift, it's like you get a lift with liquor when you ride them Greek guys. You see, they don't have jam sessions now like they used to. Before we moved from that Union Hall down there on Columbus and Playboy, it was a regular music conservatory. You could go down there and learn things, because they had guys there from everywhere playing up everything in there. You know what I mean? And the faster you get tired they would put another one on there. You know what I mean? White and color would be in there. And I mean there was so many things you could learn. You know what I'm saying? And I happened to be around some good sessions sometimes and I picked up on a lot of things. Now just like we was back there at Claiborne, I mean St. Bernard and Galvary, and I was playing back there with who? I was playing back there with a group, probably with Bud Banks and them I was playing back there with I'm not sure. And Danny Barker coming there. You understand? No I was back there with Sheik, that's right. I was back there with Cheik. Yeah I was going to ask you about that.
